property.text: The gossip validation pipeline must verify KZG proofs for data column sidecars via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs. Failure must result in REJECT. The KZG check must occur after structural validation and signature verification, but must not be skipped.

reachability.notes: An attacker modifies data column cells while keeping commitments and proofs valid-looking. If KZG verification is skipped or has implementation bugs, tampered data propagates.

property.severity_justification: Skipping or incorrectly implementing KZG proof verification allows tampered data columns to propagate through the gossip network, completely undermining data availability.
property.bug_bounty_notes: PoC: craft sidecar with tampered column data that passes KZG verification.

property.text: bytes_to_bls_field MUST reject any deserialized integer value that is greater than or equal to BLS_MODULUS. Accepting out-of-range values would produce invalid field elements, corrupting all downstream polynomial arithmetic, cell computation, and KZG proof generation.

reachability.notes: An attacker can submit blob data via type-3 transactions or send crafted cells via P2P gossip. Blob bytes are deserialized into field elements via bytes_to_bls_field in cell_to_coset_evals (SG-001). If the range check is missing, modular reduction silently corrupts data.

property.severity_justification: Violation allows an attacker to inject invalid field elements into the polynomial commitment pipeline. This corrupts KZG proofs and cells, potentially causing consensus failures where valid-looking but incorrect data passes verification across the entire network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating that an out-of-range blob byte sequence produces a cell that passes verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch but commits to incorrect data.

property.text: The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) MUST include ALL of the following in the hash input in canonical deterministic order: (1) RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN, (2) FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, (3) FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL, (4) len(commitments), (5) len(cell_indices), (6) all commitments, (7) for each k: commitment_indices[k], cell_indices[k], all coset_eval bytes, proofs[k]. Omitting any element breaks Fiat-Shamir soundness.

reachability.notes: An attacker sends crafted data column sidecars via P2P. If any verifier-relevant data is omitted from the Fiat-Shamir hash, the attacker can manipulate the omitted field while keeping the challenge r unchanged, allowing proof forgery.

property.severity_justification: Violation of Fiat-Shamir completeness breaks the soundness of the entire batch verification scheme. An attacker could forge KZG proofs that pass verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch, undermining data availability guarantees network-wide.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing a forged proof that passes batch verification due to missing Fiat-Shamir binding. This is a consensus-level vulnerability.

property.text: The RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN separator used in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) MUST be unique to this specific batch verification context and MUST NOT collide with domain separators used in any other protocol or verification context.

reachability.notes: A cross-protocol attack: if the domain separator collides with another protocol's domain, an attacker could construct a valid proof for one context and replay it in this context.

property.severity_justification: Domain separator collision could allow cross-protocol proof replay attacks, accepting proofs from unrelated contexts as valid batch KZG cell proofs.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires demonstrating a collision with another protocol's domain separator and a cross-context proof acceptance.

property.text: The hash input order in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge (SG-006) MUST be deterministic and canonical across all implementations. Two honest nodes receiving the same (commitments, cell_indices, cosets_evals, proofs) MUST compute the same challenge r.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic hash ordering would cause different nodes to compute different challenges, leading to inconsistent verification results and potential consensus splits.

property.severity_justification: Non-deterministic Fiat-Shamir challenge computation would cause consensus splits: some nodes accept a proof while others reject it, partitioning the network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating inconsistent verification results across two implementations due to ordering differences.

property.text: The universal verification equation in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) MUST satisfy: e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) where LL = g1_lincomb(proofs, r_powers), LR = KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL[n], and RL = RLC - RLI + RLP. A valid set of cells and proofs MUST always pass this check; an invalid set MUST fail with overwhelming probability (1 - 1/p).

reachability.notes: Attacker sends crafted data column sidecars. The verification equation is the final cryptographic gate. If the random challenge r has insufficient entropy or the equation is incorrectly implemented, invalid proofs could pass.

property.severity_justification: Bypassing the verification equation allows an attacker to inject invalid cells that pass verification, breaking data availability guarantees across the entire network.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating acceptance of an invalid cell-proof pair by the batch verifier.

property.text: In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015), the random challenge r MUST bind all inputs via Fiat-Shamir. The challenge MUST have full entropy of the BLS scalar field (approximately 2^255 bits). hash_to_bls_field MUST produce a uniformly random BLS field element.

reachability.notes: If the challenge r has insufficient entropy (e.g., due to weak hash or truncation), an attacker can find inputs where individual proofs are invalid but the aggregated verification equation holds.

property.severity_justification: Insufficient entropy in the random challenge directly enables proof forgery in the batch verification scheme, a network-wide consensus failure.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires analysis of hash_to_bls_field output distribution and PoC showing bias exploitation.

property.text: The commitments list passed to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) MUST contain no duplicates. Commitment deduplication in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021) MUST use byte-exact comparison, not hash-based comparison, to avoid hash collision attacks.

reachability.notes: An attacker provides commitment_bytes over P2P. If deduplication uses a weak hash, the attacker could craft two semantically different commitments that map to the same deduplicated index, causing weight aggregation errors in the verification equation.

property.severity_justification: Incorrect deduplication causes the random linear combination weights to be wrong, potentially accepting invalid proofs or rejecting valid ones.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC with crafted commitment bytes that trigger deduplication errors leading to incorrect verification results.

property.text: All commitment_indices in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl (SG-015) MUST reference valid entries in the deduplicated commitments array, i.e., forall k: commitment_indices[k] < len(commitments).

reachability.notes: Out-of-bounds commitment_indices would cause array index out-of-bounds access, potentially crashing the node.

property.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds array access could crash the validator node, causing single-node DoS.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC demonstrating node crash via crafted commitment_indices.

property.text: In verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch (SG-021), all four input lists (commitment_bytes, cell_indices, cells, proofs_bytes) MUST have equal length. Mismatched lengths MUST cause the function to reject the input before any cryptographic operations.

reachability.notes: Mismatched array lengths from P2P input could cause out-of-bounds access or incorrect verification. This is the first validation checkpoint.

property.severity_justification: Bypassing length validation could lead to out-of-bounds memory access or incorrect cryptographic results, potentially crashing the node.
property.bug_bounty_notes: Requires PoC showing crash or incorrect verification result from mismatched input lengths.
